[USER] User asks about opcodes and OP_RETURN messages, specifically Bitcoin Script fundamentals.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Assistant explains that an "opcode" is a single instruction in Bitcoin Script that specifies an operation to be performed.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Assistant provides examples of opcodes for basic mathematical operations: OP_ADD, OP_SUB, OP_MUL, OP_DIV, OP_MOD.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Assistant explains that OP_RETURN is a specific opcode that allows data to be included in the blockchain as an output of a transaction, storing up to 80 bytes of data.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Assistant describes a simple Bitcoin Script example requiring a single signature to spend a transaction.

[ASSISTANT_SAID] Assistant states that Bitcoin Script is a stack-based, Forth-like programming language used to specify conditions for spending transactions.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Assistant mentions that Bitcoin Script can be used for multi-signature transactions, time-locked transactions, and more.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Assistant explains that Bitcoin Script provides a flexible way to specify conditions for spending transactions.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Assistant concludes that studying Bitcoin Script is an important step for understanding the Bitcoin network and building applications on it.
